anchorData:
HARAMBEE HALL, GITHURAI (main phenomenon): rectangular floor, area exactly 120 m2. Width = w metres, length = (w + 2) metres. Equation: w(w + 2) = 120, which expands to w^2 + 2w - 120 = 0 (a = 1, b = 2, c = -120). Trial-and-error table (w, length, area): w=8, l=10, 80 m2 (too small); w=9, l=11, 99 m2 (too small); w=10, l=12, 120 m2 (exact); w=11, l=13, 143 m2 (too big); w=12, l=14, 168 m2 (too big). Factorised: (w + 12)(w - 10) = 0, so w = 10 or w = -12. Reject -12 because a width cannot be negative. Final hall: width 10 m, length 12 m, area 10 x 12 = 120 m2. Discriminant b^2 - 4ac = 4 + 480 = 484, sqrt = 22, w = (-2 +/- 22)/2 = 10 or -12. Why linear methods fail: w appears multiplied by itself (w x w), so it gives a w^2 term; the committee's sketch is on manila paper. Perimeter would be 2(w + w + 2) = 4w + 4, which is linear but does not give the area.

EXPANSION EXAMPLES (Lesson 2): (w + 2)(w + 3) = w^2 + 3w + 2w + 6 = w^2 + 5w + 6. (2x - 1)(3x + 4) = 6x^2 + 8x - 3x - 4 = 6x^2 + 5x - 4. KERICHO TEA-FARM PLOT: length (x + 5) m, width (x + 3) m. Area = (x + 5)(x + 3) = x^2 + 8x + 15 m2. Fencing perimeter = 2[(x + 5) + (x + 3)] = 4x + 16 m (linear, contrasts with the quadratic area). Check at x = 5: 10 m x 8 m = 80 m2 and 25 + 40 + 15 = 80.

FACTORISATION EXAMPLES (Lesson 3): x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^2 (perfect square). x^2 - 49 = (x - 7)(x + 7) (difference of two squares). 2x^2 + 7x + 3 = (2x + 1)(x + 3). Hall: w^2 + 2w - 120 = (w + 12)(w - 10), using the factor pair 12 and -10 (product -120, sum 2). GIKOMBA MANDAZI REVENUE: a vendor has (x + 3) customers each paying (x + 4) shillings, so revenue R = x^2 + 7x + 12 KES. Target R = 42 KES gives x^2 + 7x - 30 = 0 = (x + 10)(x - 3) = 0, x = 3 (reject -10); check 6 customers x 7 KES = 42.

LESSON 4 PRACTICE: KISUMU FISH POND: width w m, length (w + 3) m, area 40 m2. w^2 + 3w - 40 = 0, (w + 8)(w - 5) = 0, w = 5 (reject -8), length 8 m, 5 x 8 = 40.

NAKURU SCHOOL GARDEN (Lesson 5): width x m, length (x + 6) m, area 48 m2. x^2 + 6x = 48. It does not factorise over integers (no integer pair with product -48 and sum 6). Complete the square: x^2 + 6x + 9 = 57, (x + 3)^2 = 57, x = -3 +/- sqrt57. sqrt57 = 7.55 (2 d.p.), so x = 4.55 m (reject -10.55). Length = 10.55 m. Check: 4.55 x 10.55 = 48.0 m2 (approximately). Diagram: an x by x square plus two 3 by x rectangles, plus a 3 by 3 corner square of area 9 completes the big square of side (x + 3).

MOMBASA STONE PROBLEM (Lesson 6): a stone is thrown upward from a viewing platform 25 m above the sea. Height h = -5t^2 + 20t + 25 metres, t in seconds. Hits the sea when h = 0: -5t^2 + 20t + 25 = 0, divide by -5: t^2 - 4t - 5 = 0 = (t - 5)(t + 1). Quadratic formula: discriminant = 20^2 - 4(-5)(25) = 400 + 500 = 900, sqrt = 30, t = (-20 +/- 30)/(-10) = -1 or 5. Reject t = -1 (before the throw). The stone lands at t = 5 s. Maximum height at t = 2 s: h = -20 + 40 + 25 = 45 m.

MANDAZI PRICING (Lesson 6): Mama Wanjiru sells n = 120 - 4p mandazi a day at price p KES each. Wanted revenue p(120 - 4p) = 700 KES, so 4p^2 - 120p + 700 = 0, i.e. p^2 - 30p + 175 = 0. Discriminant = 900 - 700 = 200, sqrt200 = 14.14, p = (30 +/- 14.14)/2 = 7.93 or 22.07 KES. Both give revenue 700 mathematically (at 7.93 she sells about 88 mandazi; at 22.07 about 32). She picks the lower price because it sells more. Other discriminant examples: x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0 has discriminant 0 (one repeated solution x = 3); x^2 + 2x + 5 = 0 has discriminant -16 (no real solutions). Nakuru: x^2 + 6x - 48 = 0 has discriminant 36 + 192 = 228, x = (-6 +/- sqrt228)/2 = -3 +/- sqrt57, matching the completing-the-square result.

LESSON 7 APPLICATION PROBLEMS: (a) KITALE LAND: width w m, length (2w + 1) m, area 78 m2. 2w^2 + w - 78 = 0, (2w + 13)(w - 6) = 0, w = 6 (reject -6.5), length 13 m, 6 x 13 = 78. (b) HARAMBEE TICKET FUNDRAISING: price p KES, tickets sold = 60 - 2p, revenue 400 KES: p(60 - 2p) = 400, p^2 - 30p + 200 = 0, (p - 10)(p - 20) = 0, p = 10 (40 tickets) or p = 20 (20 tickets); both give 400, so choose 10 KES since more people attend. (c) HALL VERANDAH: a border of uniform width x m around the 12 m x 10 m hall; outer area (12 + 2x)(10 + 2x) = 168 m2, so x^2 + 11x - 12 = 0, (x + 12)(x - 1) = 0, x = 1 m (reject -12); outer rectangle 14 m x 12 m = 168.
characters: Githurai community committee (Nairobi): organises the Harambee and drew the manila-paper sketch of the hall (width = w, length = w + 2, Area = 120 m2); they are stuck using arithmetic or linear equations. Local Form 4 student (unnamed): suggests the problem needs a quadratic equation. Githurai multipurpose hall: rectangular floor, 120 m2, final size 10 m by 12 m. Kericho tea farmer: fences a rectangular plot of length (x + 5) m and width (x + 3) m (Lesson 2). Gikomba mandazi vendor (Nairobi): revenue (x + 3)(x + 4) KES (Lesson 3). Kisumu fish-pond farmer: pond with area 40 m2, length 3 m more than width (Lesson 4). Nakuru school garden club: garden with area 48 m2, length 6 m more than width (Lesson 5). Mombasa viewing platform: stone thrown from 25 m up, h = -5t^2 + 20t + 25 (Lesson 6). Mama Wanjiru (mandazi seller): demand n = 120 - 4p, wants KES 700 daily (Lesson 6). Kitale land owner, Harambee ticket committee, verandah builders: Lesson 7 problems. Students: work in pairs and groups, keep the Driving Question Board (DQB), and build the cumulative model poster.
outcome: The students and committee show that the Githurai hall equation w(w + 2) = 120 becomes w^2 + 2w - 120 = 0, which factorises as (w + 12)(w - 10) = 0 and gives w = 10 or w = -12. Only w = 10 m is physically possible, so the hall is 10 m wide and 12 m long (area 120 m2), and completing the square and the quadratic formula give the same answer. A quadratic equation can have two solutions, and context decides which one is used, so the Harambee committee can plan the hall and the community can use quadratic thinking in other planning problems.
conventions: Quadratic expression: an expression of the highest power 2, e.g. w^2 + 2w - 120. Quadratic equation: such an expression set equal to something, written in general form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0. Linear: highest power 1. Terms: a is the coefficient of x^2, b of x, c is the constant. 'Expand' means remove brackets; use both 'distributive law' and 'FOIL' (First, Outer, Inner, Last) for expansion. 'Factorise' means write as a product of brackets. Zero Product Property: if A x B = 0 then A = 0 or B = 0. Use the word 'solutions' (also called roots) for values of the unknown that satisfy the equation. Lengths in metres (m), areas in m2, money in Kenya shillings (KES), time in seconds (s). Always check each solution in the context and reject impossible ones (negative width or time). Write the quadratic formula as x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac))/(2a), with discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac: D > 0 two real solutions, D = 0 one repeated solution, D < 0 no real solutions. Hall variable is always w (width) and length is w + 2. Round decimals to 2 d.p. in final answers. Use a = -5, b = 20, c = 25 for the Mombasa stone (take g as 10 so h = -5t^2 + 20t + 25). DQB uses 'What we notice / What we wonder' cards. The three solving methods are named: (1) factorisation, (2) completing the square, (3) quadratic formula. Always state hall answers as 'width 10 m, length 12 m'.

lessonMap.focus: Predict & Anchor Phenomenon: The Githurai Harambee Hall
lessonMap.teaches: A situation where the unknown is multiplied by itself gives a quadratic equation w(w + 2) = 120 (w^2 + 2w - 120 = 0), which is different from a linear equation; the general form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 and identifying a, b, c
lessonMap.buildsOn: No earlier lesson; builds on prior knowledge of area of a rectangle and linear equations
lessonMap.usesData: Hall sketch, trial-and-error table (w = 8 to 12), w^2 + 2w - 120 = 0 with a = 1, b = 2, c = -120, perimeter 4w + 4 (linear contrast)

lessonMap.teaches: How to expand a product of two binomials using the distributive law and FOIL and collect like terms to get ax^2 + bx + c
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: the general form ax^2 + bx + c and the expression w(w + 2)
lessonMap.usesData: Expansion examples (w + 2)(w + 3) and (2x - 1)(3x + 4); Kericho tea-farm plot area x^2 + 8x + 15 and perimeter 4x + 16

lessonMap.teaches: How to reverse expansion: factorise x^2 + bx + c and ax^2 + bx + c, including perfect squares and the difference of two squares
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: expansion (FOIL) and the structure ax^2 + bx + c, used in reverse

lessonMap.teaches: The Zero Product Property: setting each factor equal to zero to find two solutions, then choosing the valid one using context
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1 and 3: the equation w^2 + 2w - 120 = 0 and its factors (w + 12)(w - 10)
lessonMap.usesData: Hall w = 10 or -12 (reject -12; 10 m by 12 m); Kisumu fish pond w^2 + 3w - 40 = 0, w = 5

lessonMap.teaches: Completing the square: rewriting x^2 + bx = k as (x + b/2)^2 = k + (b/2)^2 and taking square roots, with the area-diagram interpretation
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 2, 3 and 4: perfect square trinomials, expansion of (x + p)^2, and the idea of two solutions and context-based rejection
lessonMap.usesData: Nakuru garden x^2 + 6x = 48, (x + 3)^2 = 57, x = 4.55 m, length 10.55 m (an equation that does not factorise); diagram with a 3 by 3 corner square

lessonMap.focus: The Quadratic Formula and the Mombasa Stone Problem
lessonMap.teaches: Deriving and using x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac))/(2a) and using the discriminant to decide the number of real solutions
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 5: completing the square applied to the general form ax^2 + bx + c = 0; Lesson 4: rejecting invalid solutions
lessonMap.usesData: Mombasa stone -5t^2 + 20t + 25 = 0, D = 900, t = 5 s; Mama Wanjiru's mandazi pricing p^2 - 30p + 175 = 0, D = 200, p = 7.93 or 22.07 KES; hall D = 484 check; discriminant examples D = 0 and D = -16

lessonMap.teaches: Choosing and justifying the most efficient solving method in new contexts, and assembling a cumulative model that closes the DQB (no new technique)
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1 to 6: all three methods and the idea that context selects the valid solution
lessonMap.usesData: Full hall problem solved three ways (w = 10, length 12); Kitale land 2w^2 + w - 78 = 0 (w = 6, length 13); ticket revenue p^2 - 30p + 200 = 0 (p = 10 or 20); hall verandah x^2 + 11x - 12 = 0 (x = 1 m)
